right coronary arterial flow dynamics are strongly influenced by dominance, systemic and pulmonary hypertension, and the presence of left or right ventricular hypertrophy, whereas left coronary arterial and microvascular flow patterns are less affected.
the effects of coronary arterial dominance and systemic/papmonary hypertension on coronary hemodynamics are complex and regionally dependent.
the effects of left and right dominance on regional coronary flow patterns vary depending on the presence and type of hypertension.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coronary hemodynamics are influenced by the anatomical dominance and by the presence of hypertension.
coronary dominance and hypertension have a profound impact on the regional coronary hemodynamics and the effects are different for left and right coronary circulation.
the effects of left coronary artery dominance on the regional coronary hemodynamics is not as pronounced as the effect of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coronary arterial dominance and the hypertension are important factors that affect the regional coronary hemodynamics.
left coronary artery dominance is associated with higher coronary flow and lower wall shear stress than right coronary artery dominance.
coronary arterial dominance and systemic and pulmonary hypertension are important determinants of coronary flow dynamics and should be considered in the context of coronary risk assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of coronary dominance on coronary flow patterns are complex and depend on the specific combination of intravascular and transmural conditions.

right dominance and hypertension are associated with a greater risk for ischemia in the right ventricular and right ventricular septum, which may explain why right ventricular infarctions are more prevalent than left ventricular infarcts.
